rationale: This sample is a hot numeric benchmark (ooura FFT) where nearly all execution time is spent in tight FP loops inside cftmdl, cft1st, and cdft, so runtime-expensive passes must be suppressed: BCF is effectively disabled (low RuntimeCost/SizeCost tolerance) since bogus control flow would bloat the 18KB text section and break FP vectorization in the hottest loops, and IBR is kept low because indirect branches serialize hot-loop dispatch. FLA is given the highest security weight since flattening the large, complex CFG of cftmdl (12KB, the dominant function) yields the biggest reverse-engineering resistance, but its low RuntimeCost weight ensures it is reserved for the few large cold-ish functions rather than the inner FFT kernels. SUB is favored strongly across cost dimensions because arithmetic substitution is cheap and its main caution is FP-vectorization interference, so moderate security/diversity with high cost tolerance lets it apply broadly. SPLIT and IGV are low-cost enablers (SPLIT improves the effectiveness of the limited FLA use; IGV hides ooura's global trig tables) and receive healthy cost tolerances, while ICALL gets low security/diversity weight because this program is mostly straight-line numeric code with very few indirect-call-worthy sites, making indirection there pure overhead with negligible RE payoff. CorrectnessRisk tolerances are kept highest for SUB/SPLIT/IGV (semantics-preserving by construction) and moderate for FLA/IBR/ICALL, which restructure control flow and can disturb sensitive code like the bitrv2 permutation logic.
